ITEM_A_negative_control.verdict: DETECTOR FIRES - but only on ONE of its four clauses. The other three PASS on a genuine CRM failure. See critical_finding.

mechanism_used.chosen: Fixture-controlled induced CRM failure. `sorento-sub-respond-findcontact-respond` is a Code node whose entire body is `return $('redis-pop-main-message-list').first().json.message.contact`, so the redis item's contact.id flows verbatim into every CRM node URL. Setting contact.id='000000000000' makes the real CRM return a real 404 to the real node, over the real credential.
mechanism_used.why_not_credential_edit: Explicitly forbidden by the task and by the harness rules. No credential was created, bound, or altered.
mechanism_used.why_not_test_workflow_pinData: Attempted and rejected on two grounds, both reported rather than worked around. (1) STRUCTURAL: test_workflow's pinData type is {nodeName: Array<{json:...}>} - a flat item array. That maps to main[0] only. There is NO representation for main[1] and NO representation for the runData `error` object. pinData therefore CANNOT express the continueErrorOutput dead-end, which is the exact failure mode the reviewer asked to be proven. The reviewer's named cheap mechanism is not capable of producing the failure it was proposed to detect. (2) SAFETY: prepare_test_pin_data(txiPzSxy3Pclsz6v) reports 105 of 135 nodes 'skipped' - they execute FOR REAL under test_workflow - and that set includes every egress-capable executeWorkflow caller (8x sorento-sub-respond-sendmsg-respond*, Call 'sub-human-intervention'). Running the full clone through an unproven vehicle with 24 schema-less nodes to hand-invent is a materially larger egress surface than the established zz-canary-run path, and per LESSONS 47 pinning cannot be pre-asserted. Not run.
mechanism_used.note_on_401_vs_404: The induced failure is a 404, not a 401. This does not weaken the result: n8n wraps ANY non-2xx from an HTTP node into the same runData envelope, discriminated only by the `status` field. A 401 produces a byte-identical structure with status:401. The discriminator reads shape, not cause.

ITEM_A_negative_control.the_assertion_under_test: executionStatus=='success' AND error==null AND main[0] carries a domain-specific key no auth-error envelope can contain AND main[1] empty

FAILED_RUN.EXECUTION_status: success  <-- the execution does NOT report error
FAILED_RUN.clause_3_domain_key_present: FAIL  <-- the only clause that catches it (no respond_io_id / no session_vars)
FAILED_RUN.downstream_corruption_observed: The downstream Code node `get-session-vars` consumed the AxiosError envelope AS IF IT WERE SESSION DATA and passed it on. This empirically confirms plan CORRECTION 3's stated 'worst case' for continueRegularOutput, which had until now only been asserted.

critical_finding.headline: THREE OF THE FOUR DISCRIMINATOR CLAUSES ARE DECORATIVE. Only clause 3 (domain-specific key in main[0]) is an instrument.
critical_finding.detail: On a node with onError=continueRegularOutput - which on the clone is get-session-vars-http, and which plan CORRECTION 3 already calls the worst case - a genuine CRM failure yields node executionStatus='success', error=null, main[0] populated (with garbage), and main[1] empty. Three clauses pass. If a future tester scored auth conversion on 'executionStatus success + error null + main[1] empty' and did not inspect the BODY, they would score a 404/401 as a PASS.
critical_finding.consequence: The T0 verification approach is SOUND, but only because the T0 tester happened to record a body_excerpt per node and the reviewer explicitly reasoned on payload shape ('a 401 body cannot contain {"allowed":true}'). The reviewer's own instinct was right and is now measured: payload shape IS the proof, and the surrounding three clauses add no detection power. They must not be treated as independent corroboration.
critical_finding.recommendation: Restate the T1-T5 acceptance predicate as a single mandatory clause: main[0] must carry a named, per-node, domain-specific key (a checklist of which key per node), and must NOT carry a top-level `error` key. Drop executionStatus/error/main[1] from the PASS criteria, or demote them to informational. Add an explicit negative assertion: main[0][0].json.error must be absent.

what_could_NOT_be_proven.gap: The continueErrorOutput dead-end (get-access-types, get-presigned-url) was NOT induced. Recorded as unverified per LESSONS 54 - never inferred from a clean run.
what_could_NOT_be_proven.why: Both nodes interpolate the SAME `$('sorento-sub-respond-findcontact-respond').first().json.id` that check-access-http uses. A contact id bad enough to fail them also makes check-access-http return a legitimate 2xx denial ({allowed:false, decision:'deny_unknown_contact'} - observed, exec 9456578), so If5 routes to the no-access branch and neither node is ever reached. There is no fixture value that fails one and not the other. get-presigned-url's inputs come from get-results attachments and are not fixture-addressable at all.
what_could_NOT_be_proven.what_IS_known_about_that_shape: From two real errored nodes in this clone: exec 9445222 (`Call 'sub-respond-save-message-redis'2`, NodeOperationError) and exec 9445575 (`construct-user-prompt`, TypeError). In BOTH, the failing node's runData entry carries executionStatus='error', a populated `error` object (13 keys: context/errorResponse/executionId/functionality/level/message/messages/name/node/stack/tags/timestamp/workflowId), and `data` ABSENT entirely (no main at all). INFERENCE, clearly labelled as such: n8n records a failing node's runData entry identically regardless of onError; onError governs only whether the EXECUTION continues and where the error item is routed. If that holds, clauses 1, 2 and 3 all fire on a continueErrorOutput failure and the detector is sound there too. This is an inference from two real observations, NOT a measurement, and it is the one remaining hole.
what_could_NOT_be_proven.how_to_close_it_cheaply: Requires a node-level lever the harness does not currently have. The honest options are (a) a purpose-built harness workflow containing one HTTP node with onError=continueErrorOutput and main[1] unwired, pointed at an unroutable address (e.g. 127.0.0.1:9) - zero network egress, establishes the n8n mechanic authoritatively, but is a replica rather than the real node; or (b) a second CRM credential holding a deliberately-invalid key, which MCP cannot create (LESSONS 2) and which would need the user to add in the n8n UI. Recommend (b) as a one-off harness asset before T5, since it also makes a real 401 reproducible on demand for the live spine's three dead-end nodes.

safety.note: The induced failure is a READ with a nonexistent identifier. It mutates nothing. The CRM answered 404 'Respond contact not found' - no record was created, modified or probed for secrets, and the correct credential was used throughout (this is not a credential-probing exercise).
